fees: Minneapolis (city-published, minneapolismn.gov): standard tow $222; heavy-duty tow $224.50; winch-out $124.50 per half hour; storage $18 per day; notification letter $6. Other cities set their own rates; storage charges pile up daily, so ask the lot for the current total before you go.
find_car: In Minneapolis, the car is at the Minneapolis Impound Lot, 51 N. Colfax Ave. N. Call the lot to confirm it is there and ask what to bring. The registered owner must show a driver's license or other government-issued photo ID and proof of ownership (title or registration). If five or more unpaid citations are owed, the car cannot be released until the fines are paid or a Hennepin County Violations Bureau letter is obtained. Booted cars are towed within 24 to 72 hours. Elsewhere in Minnesota, contact the police department or sheriff's office that ordered the tow to learn which lot holds the vehicle.

unclaimed: If a vehicle is not reclaimed within 30 days after notification by certified mail or prescribed publication, the sheriff of the county or the city police of the city in which the vehicle is being stored may sell it at public auction (Mont. Code Ann. 61-12-404). When a vehicle is taken into custody as a result of the arrest of the driver, the owner, lienholder, or person entitled to possession has 60 days after notification to reclaim it before it may be considered abandoned and sold. After a sale, the former owner has no further right, title, claim, or interest in the vehicle.
